title: Dianelle Martinez Calls Downtown 'Dead,' Questions Business Improvement District Results
excerpt: Community leader Dianelle Martinez criticized conditions in downtown Laredo and questioned what the downtown Business Improvement District has done with the money it has collected, in a recent podcast appearance. She defended Mayor Dr. Victor D. Treviño bringing the matter before City Council.
content:
Community leader Dianelle Martinez criticized conditions in downtown Laredo and questioned what the downtown Business Improvement District has done with the money it has collected.

In a recent podcast appearance, Martinez said downtown is “dead” and asked what the district has done with the money collected from downtown commercial property owners. She said only a street or two appear lit up, and questioned the district’s accountability, preparedness and measurable results.

Martinez said the district traces to legislation from 2013, was dormant for about a decade, and has only recently begun collecting money. She defended Mayor Dr. Victor D. Treviño’s decision to bring the matter before City Council, saying the discussion exposed shortcomings in the district’s presentation and gave residents a chance to examine how it operates.

Downtown Laredo sits in District 8, represented by Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa, who faces Treviño in the mayoral runoff on Dec. 12.

The City Council voted on Nov. 16 to keep the business improvement district in place, with city staff to report back by February on fees and concerns about liens and foreclosures, and a confidential survey of the commercial property owners who pay into it. The district was created in 2021 and began providing services in 2026. It collected about $276,000 for the 2025 assessment year and spent about $30,000 to launch the district and begin services, with the remaining funds supporting cleaning, lighting and streetscape upkeep.
